title: Molecular Mechanism of the N501Y Mutation for Enhanced Binding between SARS-CoV-2’s Spike Protein and Human ACE2 Receptor
authors: Binquan Luan; Haoran Wang; Tien Huynh
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子MD模拟研究SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白N501Y突变增强与ACE2结合，虽属蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA体系，但MD方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模，相关性有限。
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been an ongoing global pandemic for over a year. Recently, an emergent SARS-CoV-2 variant (B.1.1.7) with an unusually large number of mutations had become highly contagious and wide-spreading in United Kingdom. From genome analysis, the N501Y mutation within the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2’s spike protein might have enhanced the viral protein’s binding with the human angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (hACE2). The latter is the prelude for the virus’ entry into host cells. So far, the molecular mechanism of this enhanced binding is still elusive, which prevents us from assessing its effects on existing therapeutic antibodies. Using all atom molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrated that Y501 in mutated RBD can be well coordinated by Y41 and K353 in hACE2 through hydrophobic interactions, increasing the overall binding affinity between RBD and hACE2 by about 0.81 kcal/mol. We further explored how the N501Y mutation might affect the binding between a neutralizing antibody (CB6) and RBD. We expect that our work can help researchers design proper measures responding to this urgent virus mutation, such as adding a modified/new neutralizing antibody specifically targeting at this variant in the therapeutic antibody cocktail. abstract_zh: 2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）已持续全球大流行超过一年。近期，一种具有异常大量突变的新兴SARS-CoV-2变异株（B.1.1.7）在英国表现出高度传染性并广泛传播。通过基因组分析，SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白受体结合域（RBD）中的N501Y突变可能增强了该病毒蛋白与人类血管紧张素转换酶2（hACE2）的结合，后者是病毒进入宿主细胞的前奏。迄今为止，这种增强结合的分子机制仍不明确，这阻碍了我们评估其对现有治疗性抗体的影响。利用全原子分子动力学模拟，我们证明突变型RBD中的Y501可通过疏水相互作用与hACE2中的Y41和K353良好协调，使RBD与hACE2之间的整体结合亲和力增加约0.81 kcal/mol。我们进一步探讨了N501Y突变可能如何影响中和抗体（CB6）与RBD之间的结合。我们期望我们的工作能帮助研究人员制定应对这一紧急病毒突变的适当措施，例如在治疗性抗体鸡尾酒中添加一种针对该变异株的修饰或新型中和抗体。摘要图
